claims.text: MoNbTaW is a Ta-containing refractory high-entropy alloy relevant to the proposed BCC target class.
Standard experimental melting-property measurements are infeasible for the target alloy.
Replacing full ab initio thermodynamic integration with an MLP-based perturbation scheme will retain accurate phase-transition free-energy differences.
Validation against SRO-dependent elastic constants and VDOS is more informative for free-energy accuracy than validation against bulk lattice parameters alone.
A moment tensor potential can be combined with hybrid MD/Monte Carlo to generate and simulate random and SRO states in MoNbTaW.
Explicit inclusion of varying-SRO configurations and ordered clusters in the MLP training set is required for accurate free-energy calculations.
MD coupled with Monte Carlo swaps can sample the evolution of chemical SRO.
Temperatures of 2000–3000 K are near the target alloy's melting point and lie in a pressure-temperature region where BCC is stable.
SRO can produce ordered clusters in refractory BCC high-entropy alloys.
SRO and ordered-phase formation reduce lattice distortion or atomic displacement.
SRO and transient ordered clusters alter the vibrational density of states.
SRO is the primary mediator of the free-energy difference between random and ordered states in the target alloy.
SRO has measurable, temperature-dependent effects in MoNbTaW, including approximately 180 MPa extra screw-dislocation strengthening at 300 K and negligible strengthening at 2000 K.
The MLP captures energy barriers for breaking local chemical order, including the creation of diffuse antiphase boundaries and stabilization of ordered clusters.
Standard EAM potentials fail to represent the SRO-dependent stabilization and complex liquid structure of the target multicomponent alloy.
SRO-induced changes in vibrational entropy and enthalpy drive the relevant free-energy difference.
The proposed method will predict melting temperature within 50–100 K of high-fidelity ab initio benchmarks.
Standard EAM predictions will deviate by more than 200 K because they omit SRO-dependent solid stabilization.
The MLP-based perturbation method will reduce computational cost by an order of magnitude relative to full DFT thermodynamic integration.

An MLP trained only on ground-state or low-temperature SRO configurations may fail to extrapolate to the high-temperature liquid, and rare high-energy SRO fluctuations may be undersampled by TOR-TILD-like approaches.
